startup.name: Context.dev
startup.description: Context.dev provides structured data from any website through one API for AI agents and developer products. It states it powers Mintlify, Super, Vizzy, Klarna and more than 800 companies. Revenue comes from API usage by developers.

yc_acceptance.basis: Note only: already accepted to YC Summer 2026, so this is not a forecast. Prior for a random applicant is about 1 percent (yc_acceptance.md). Claimed 800 plus customers is strong traction.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: Not applicable since the company was accepted. YC would most plausibly worry that web data APIs are crowded by Firecrawl, Exa, Apify and Bright Data, and that the customer count lacks revenue depth. Because acceptance is already a fact in this test, the estimate is a placeholder and the forecast value sits in the funding ladder that follows.

ladder.why_it_fails: Seed stalls if the 800 customers are mostly free or very small and revenue stays low, or if the team of six is distracted. Dashblock, a website to API company from 2019, shut down, and Anakin raised only a 2M seed before slow growth. Investors at this step want proof that growth, retention and margins hold up against better funded rivals, and a weak showing on any of them ends the path here, as the analogs listed in this evaluation show.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The most common ends are a small acquisition by a data or developer platform, or a stall as search and browsing become features of model providers. A large exit needs category leadership. A meaningful exit needs a durable lead in a category where rivals can copy features and raise more money, and most companies in the reference cohort stay small, are acquired cheaply or stop operating before that point.

killers.risk: Firecrawl, Exa and others win the category
killers.evidence: Exa raised a large Series C in May 2026 and Firecrawl raised a Series A in 2025 with many developers.
killers.mitigation: Focus on structured outputs and reliability for named verticals.

killers.risk: Models and agent platforms add built in web access
killers.evidence: Search and browsing tools already ship inside major model APIs, which reduces the need for a separate vendor.
killers.mitigation: Offer freshness, schemas and guarantees that general tools lack.

killers.risk: Anti bot and legal pressure raise costs
killers.evidence: Scraping at scale depends on proxies and on site tolerance, and blocking raises cost per request.
killers.mitigation: Build licensed data partnerships and caching.

technical_complexity.rationale: Scraping, extraction with models and caching are buildable by a small team. The hard part is staying reliable against blocking at scale and keeping cost per request low.

takeover_risk.rationale: Funded rivals can match features in months and model providers can bundle browsing; the defense is customer lock in via structured schemas and integrations.

brand.name: Context.dev
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Context.dev" --era 2022+: 7 characters, 2 syllables, real word
strengths: Fits the agent context theme and is a real word
weaknesses: Generic, hard to own in search
brand.rationale: Descriptive developer brand names such as Firecrawl and Browserbase work when the product is strong, and a .dev style name signals a developer audience, a small plus.

narrative.headline: Strong early pull in a crowded and well funded category; seed is likely, later rounds depend on beating Firecrawl and Exa.
narrative.general_summary: Context.dev starts the batch with claimed usage by hundreds of companies, which is unusual and lifts seed odds above the cohort. The category is hot, but the leaders have raised far more and model providers can bundle web access. The outcome hinges on whether it carves out structured data and reliability as a distinct product. The forecast treats the day one description as the best case, anchors on the 2022 to 2024 cohort of researched YC companies, and widens the uncertainty because funding data for recent batches is incomplete and right censored.

assumptions: Pretend date is 2026-07-06 and only the input file describes the company.
Seed means a round above about 500K within about 12 months of batch start.
The 800 customer claim is taken as stated but not verified, and may include free users.
